listen_text: Section. Rules and Derivations. For the following, let Gamma, Delta, Pi, and Lambda represent finite sequences of sentences. Definition. Sequent. An n -sided sequent is an expression of the form Displayed expression. the n sided sequent whose positions, in order, contain Gamma sub one through Gamma sub n. End displayed expression. where each Gamma sub one is a finite (possibly empty) sequences of sentences of the language L . End definition. Source anomaly note. The source says each Gamma sub one and uses the plural sequences after a singular subject. Its displayed n sided list and definition concern one finite sequence at each position. These wording defects are retained with this note. Original source remains available in Source view. End note. Definition. Initial Sequent. An n -sided initial sequent is an n -sided sequent of the form the n sided sequent with formula A alone in every position for any sentence A in the language. If the language contains a zero place connective star , that is, a propositional constant, then we also take the sequent with star in one position where the propositional constant star appears in the space for the truth value associated with the truth value assigned by the nullary truth function for star, which belongs to V , and is empty otherwise. End definition. For each connective of an n valued logic L , there is a logical rule for each truth value that this connective can take in logic L . Derivations in an n -sided sequent calculus for logic L are trees of sequents, where the topmost sequents are initial sequents, and if a sequent stands below one or more other sequents, it must follow correctly by a rule of inference for the connectives of logic L . Definition. Theorems. A sentence A is a theorem of an n valued logic L if there is a derivation of the n -sequent containing formula A in each position corresponding to a designated truth value of logic L . We write formula A is a theorem of logic L if formula A is a theorem and formula A is not a theorem of logic L if it is not. End definition. Definition. Derivability. A sentence A is derivable from a set of sentences Gamma in an n valued logic L , formula A is derivable from Gamma in logic L , if and only if there is a finite subset Gamma sub zero of Gamma and a sequence Gamma sub zero prime of the sentences in Gamma sub zero such that the following sequent has a derivation: Displayed expression. the n sided sequent whose positions, in order, contain Lambda sub one through Lambda sub n. End displayed expression. where Lambda sub i is formula A if position i corresponds to a designated truth value, and Gamma sub zero prime otherwise. If formula A is not derivable from Gamma we write formula A is not derivable from Gamma . End definition. For instance, three valued Łukasiewicz logic has a three -sided sequent calculus. In a three -sided sequent with Gamma in the false position, Pi in the middle position, and Delta in the true position , Gamma corresponds to the false truth value , Delta to the true truth value , and Pi to the middle truth value . Axioms are all three sided sequents with formula A in every position . Since only the true truth value is designated, formula A is derivable from Gamma in three valued Lukasiewicz logic if and only if the sequent with Gamma in the false position, Gamma in the middle position, and A in the true position has a derivation. (If the middle truth value were also designated, we would need a derivation of the three sided sequent with false position Gamma; middle position formula A; and true position formula A .) End section.

listen_text: Section. Propositional Rules for Selected Logics. The inference rules for a connective in an n -sided sequent calculus only depend on the characteristic truth function for the connective. Thus, if some connective is defined by the same truth function in different logics, these n -sided sequent rules for the connective are the same in those logics. Section. Rules for negation . The following rules for negation apply to Łukasiewicz and Kleene logics, and their variants. Proof tree. False position negation rule for Lukasiewicz and Kleene logics. Premise node one: the three sided sequent with false position Gamma; middle position Pi; and true position Delta, followed by formula A .
